answer: Each epoch, answers arrive sealed: an account first posts a hash on a public ledge, and reveals the text behind it only after the round closes, a quill unwrapped at dawn. Revealed texts are compared pairwise, and identities whose words overlap beyond a threshold count as one author: both lose their bonds and their weight collapses to a single seat. A farm commits k hashes cheaply but cannot reveal k genuinely different texts without k authoring processes, and any shared wording links the batch. The k-th identity costs a distinct text and a bond that dies on duplication, not another envelope.
